system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Page counts (en 3, ar 6) are within the 15-page maximum, and the encodings are correct: GSM-7 for English, UCS-2 for Arabic. Two problems remain. First, both languages open with EXERCISE/تمرين but end with 'This is not a drill'/'هذا ليس تمريناً', so a reader cannot tell whether this is real. Exercise and live alerts also go out under different CMAS message identifiers. A person must decide which one this is. Second, neither language gives any protective action, so the first page carries the hazard but no action.

objections.issue: The message contradicts itself on whether it is an exercise. It opens with 'EXERCISE' and ends with 'This is not a drill.' The Arabic does the same ('تمرين' … 'هذا ليس تمريناً'). Handsets receive exercise alerts under a separate CMAS Exercise message identifier, so a person must decide whether this is an exercise or a live alert before broadcast.
objections.fix: An authorised person decides whether this is an exercise or a live alert. Remove the contradicting phrase in both languages and use the matching message identifier (CMAS Exercise 4381/4394 if it is an exercise).

evidence.quote: CMAS CBS Message Identifier for CMAS Exercise.

objections.issue: Neither language contains a protective action. The text describes the dust and sand hazard and how long it will last, but does not tell people what to do. The first page therefore does not carry the action.
objections.fix: Add a short protective action early in both languages, ideally on the first page. For example: 'Avoid driving; if you must, slow down and use low-beam lights. People with respiratory conditions should stay indoors.' Add the equivalent in Arabic.
